headline: Future, the UK publisher of Tom's Guide and Techradar, is cutting more jobs and blames falling search traffic, which Press Gazette ties to Google's AI Overviews.
score_reason: Lowered 1 from the pool score 5: the Android Central layoffs were reported on 1 Oct; Press Gazette adds the memo and audience data.
importance_line: Staff at the affected sites are hit first, then publishers that depend on Google traffic, but the number of roles at risk is unclear and Future's memo blames the decline in search in general, so the AI Overviews link is Press Gazette's reading of the data.
summary: Press Gazette reports, from a memo it has seen from chief executive Kevin Li Ying, that staff at Future's Android Central, Tom's Guide and Techradar in the UK, US and Canada were told last week that their roles are at risk, the second round of cuts this year after 45 editorial redundancies in January. Ipsos data cited by Press Gazette show Techradar's UK audience down 35% and Tom's Guide's down 55% since July 2024, the month before Google's AI Overviews (AI-written answers above search results) launched there; The Verge reported on 1 Oct that Android Central had laid off all its staff, though Future says the site will continue.
notes: Read in full. Press Gazette's own reporting (memo seen by the outlet, Future statements). The Android Central layoffs first surfaced on 1 Oct via The Verge, so the event predates the window; hold back as stale unless the new memo and audience data are wanted.
